sections.title: Youth Expertise: Young People in Knowledge Production and Institutional Change (A)
sections.description: Young people are deeply affected by decisions made about schools and communities, yet they are rarely recognized as experts in shaping those decisions. This Academically-Based Community Service (ABCS) course asks: What shifts when those closest to an issue are recognized as experts in defining problems, producing knowledge, and shaping the decisions that govern their lives? With a focus on children, adolescents, and young adults in the context of urban education, we will examine how expertise is recognized, contested, and mobilized within public life and educational institutions. Students will interrogate how expertise is socially constructed; how young people's claims to expertise are shaped by power and inequality; and how the politics of expertise influence decision-making within schools and other public institutions. Using our West Philadelphia neighborhood as a primary case, students will examine urban education as a sociological case through which to explore race, class, neighborhood inequality, governance, and the relationships among schools, community organizations, and public institutions. We will examine historical and contemporary efforts to center youth expertise, including youth organizing and youth participatory action research. Students will work alongside a group of high school students engaged in youth participatory evaluation of their own youth leadership program. Together, university and high school students will investigate how institutional authority is negotiated when young people are recognized as knowledge producers and decision makers, and what these shifts reveal about expertise, participation, and social change. This is an ABCS course.
